# Yuku, a JavaScript/TypeScript Compiler Toolchain in Zig

> Yuku is a high-performance JavaScript and TypeScript compiler toolchain written in Zig.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](https://yuku.fyi/): Yuku is a high-performance JavaScript and TypeScript compiler toolchain written in Zig.
- [Parser](https://yuku.fyi/parser/): A fast, spec-compliant JavaScript and TypeScript parser written in Zig.
- [AST](https://yuku.fyi/parser/ast/): The flat, data-oriented AST Yuku's parser produces, with its comments and tokens.
- [Semantic Analysis](https://yuku.fyi/parser/semantic/): Scopes, symbols, resolved references, early errors, and module records for a parsed tree.
- [Traverse](https://yuku.fyi/parser/traverse/): Walk and transform a tree with typed visitor hooks, in four modes from plain visits to full semantics.
- [Codegen](https://yuku.fyi/parser/codegen/): Print a tree back to JavaScript or TypeScript source, with type stripping, minification, and source maps.
- [Testing](https://yuku.fyi/testing/): How Yuku is tested: the parser test suite, exact AST validation, codegen conformance, semantic analysis against TypeScript, and fuzzing.
- [Security](https://yuku.fyi/security/): How to report a vulnerability in Yuku, and the security practices behind the toolchain and its releases.
